newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria establishes oil, gas export zone.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria establishes oil, gas export zone.

text.p: Nigeria's Minister of Commerce and Tourism Rear Admiral Jubrila Ayinla on Tuesday said the military government had issued a decree establishing an oil and gas export free-zone in the southeastern town of Onne-Ikpokiri.

"The establishment of the oil and gas free-zone is a further demonstration of this administration's desire to create conducive investment climate in the oil and gas sector of the economy," Ayinla said, quoted by News Agency of Nigeria.

The zone, which will provide a self-regulatory economic zone where goods would be produced primarily for the export market, is aimed at encouraging foreign investment and diversifying Nigeria's oil-dependent economy.
Nigeria has reiterated that it wants to privatise its oil and gas sector.
But Ayinla said the creation of the new free zone was for a different purpose.

"It is expected that when fully operational, the new oil and gas export free zone will increase commercial and investment portfolio of the upstream sector of the oil industry which is yet to enjoy a boom," he said.
Construction of an export processing zone (EPZ) is nearing completion in the southeastern city of Calabar.
Nigeria, Africa's largest oil producer, currently derives more than 90 percent of its foreign exchange earnings from oil exports. -- Lagos newsroom +234 1 263 03 17
